title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Review & Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary

This page defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and runbook structure. The intent is to provide a single, prescriptive reference SRE teams and service owners can use to maintain consistent reliability posture across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope

Applies to all externally-facing Redwood services and infra components that are on-call-managed by SRE or a product team with an assigned SRE contact. This includes API frontends, model-serving clusters, routing and caching layers, auth/billing, and telemetry pipelines.

Goals

- Standardize SLO definition and error budget policy so product teams make consistent tradeoffs.
- Ensure capacity planning is proactive and aligns with customer SLAs and business forecasts.
- Maintain a blameless, timely incident review process that drives systemic fixes.
- Provide operational tooling and runbook templates that reduce MTTx (detection/response/recovery).

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Principles

- SLOs measure user-facing reliability (availability, latency, correctness) rather than internal metrics.
- Every public API or customer-visible service must have at least one SLO and a documented measurement method.
- Error budgets are the primary mechanism to balance reliability vs velocity. Exhausting an error budget triggers mitigation actions.

SLO Format and Minimum Metadata (required fields)

- title: short descriptive name (e.g. API: generation.success-rate)
- owner: product or SRE team owning the SLO
- objective: numeric SLO (e.g. 99.95%) and measurement window (30d, 90d, or 1y)
- metric: query name and principal instrumentation (PromQL / ClickHouse SQL)
- numerator / denominator definitions
- alerting thresholds (warning and critical tied to remaining error budget %)
- measurement window and burn-rate policy
- consequences and mitigation policy when budget is exceeded

Example SLOs (recommended defaults)

- API availability (primary): success rate >= 99.95% over 30d window (numerator = 2xx/3xx responses; denominator = total requests).
- API p95 latency (secondary): p95 <= 300ms for token-less control-plane calls over 30d window.
- Model generation tail latency: p99 <= 2.5s for <= 1024 token requests for hosted tier.
- Inference correctness (for eval-backed routes): pass-rate on canonical prompt set >= 98% over 30d.

Error Budget Policy

- Error budget = 1 - objective. For example, 0.05% monthly for 99.95%.
- Burn analysis: automatically compute 1d, 7d, and 30d burn rates and surface both in dashboards and in weekly reliability reports.
- Actions by remaining budget:
  - > 75% remaining: standard ops. No restrictions.
  - 50-75% remaining: engineering works to prioritize reliability fixes in next sprint; product notified.
  - 25-50% remaining: restrict non-essential rollouts and schedule a reliability sync with SRE.
  - < 25% remaining: freeze risky deployments; perform immediate mitigation runbook; scope a postmortem for cause analysis.
  - 0%: emergency escalation to incident response and CEO-notification for customer-impacting services with SLA commitments.

SLO Review Cadence

- Quarterly review between product, SRE, and observability to confirm objectives remain appropriate.
- Any SLO change requires owner justification, SRE sign-off, and a 30d notice window for customers if it reduces reliability guarantees.

2) Capacity Planning

Forecasting & Targets

- Annual capacity forecasts are derived from product usage projections + 25% safety margin by default. For headroom-sensitive components (model-serving GPUs), use 40% margin unless financial tradeoffs are documented.
- Monthly capacity check-ins: compare realized growth to forecast and trigger procurement or scaling if delta > 10% sustained over 2 weeks.

Sizing & Scaling Policies

- Define minimum and target capacity tiers: baseline (N), burst (N+X) and degraded mode (N-1) with clear perf impact.
- Autoscaling thresholds: CPU/GPU utilization target is 65-75%; scale-out at sustained 75% over 5m, scale-in when < 45% for 10m.
- Queue depth and request backlog thresholds must map to SLO degradation tolerance.

Operational Procedures

- Capacity runbooks must include: current inventories (hosts/GPUs), allocation per customer tier, expected time-to-provision (cloud vs on-prem), and rollback plan for new capacity faults.
- Procurement playbook: triggers, approvers, and timeline for reserved capacity purchases.

3) Reliability Initiatives and Toil Reduction

Program Structure

- Each quarter SRE maintains a 60/40 split between reliability initiatives (60%) and operational responsiveness (40%). Initiatives are tracked in the reliability roadmap and tagged to measurable OKRs (MTTR, error-budget burn reduction, mean capacity headroom).

Typical Initiatives

- Automatic pre-warming and caching improvements for heavy prompt patterns.
- KV and prefix cache persistence across restarts to reduce cold-start latency.
- Query-level adaptive batching to preserve latency SLO while improving cost.
- Alert de-duplication and noise suppression to reduce page frequency by target of 30% YoY.

4) Incident Review Standards (Postmortems)

Culture and Timeline

- All Sev2+ incidents that impact SLOs must have a postmortem within 7 business days. Follow-up fixes should be tracked and completed or reprioritized within 90 days.
- Postmortems are blameless, focus on systemic causes, and include a clear action plan with owners and deadlines.

Postmortem Template (required fields)

- incident_id: unique identifier
- severity: Sev1 | Sev2 | Sev3
- summary: one-paragraph impact summary
- timeline: ordered timestamps and events (detection, mitigation steps, recovery)
- root cause: concise explanation of root cause(s)
- contributing factors: list of systemic issues or gaps
- remediation: immediate mitigation, short-term mitigation, long-term fix(s) with owners and ETA
- lessons learned: what will be done differently
- verification plan: how we will confirm fix effectiveness

Review Process

- Incident author submits draft within 3 business days, SRE reviews within 5 business days, and final postmortem published within 7 business days.
- For product-impacting incidents, invite Product, Security, and Customer Success to the review.

Severity Classification Guidance

- Sev1: Major customer impact across >= 25% of customers, or violation of SLA commitments resulting in contractual credit. Requires page to on-call and exec notification.
- Sev2: Partial degradation impacting >= 5% customers or core functionality; requires on-call and SRE lead engagement.
- Sev3: Minor customer impact, single-customer issue, or internal-only degradation.

5) Operational Tooling and Observability

Dashboarding

- Standard dashboard set for each service: Traffic, Errors, Latency (p50/p95/p99), Resource utilization (CPU/GPU/Memory), Queue depth, Cache hit-rate, and SLO burn charts.
- Dashboards must include drill-down links to traces and raw logs for the last 72 hours.

Alerting Standards

- Every alert must specify: symptom, owner, runbook link, and expected paging policy. Use severity labels (P1/P2/P3) mapped to on-call rotations.
- Paging thresholds should be tied to user impact. Avoid paging for minor internal anomalies; use aggregated and grouped alerts where appropriate.

Automations and Runbook Integration

- Integrate runbooks with PagerDuty/Slack: alert payloads should contain a runbook URL and suggested remediation commands.
- Automate repetitive mitigations (e.g., rolling restart, cache purge, temporary scale-up) as safe-playbooks with one-click run buttons in the console.

6) SRE Runbooks (Structure & Examples)

Runbook Structure (required sections)

1. Title and scope
2. Responsible on-call role and escalation path
3. Symptoms and detection signals
4. Quick triage checklist (5 bullet steps)
5. Remediation steps (ordered)
6. Post-incident tasks and verification
7. Links to dashboards, logs, and related runbooks
8. Last tested date and owner

Example: API: Degraded Response Rate (Runbook excerpt)

- Title: API Degraded Response Rate
- Scope: User-facing text generation API (hosted and dedicated frontends)
- Owner: API Platform SRE
- Symptoms: p95 latency >= 1.5s for 10m or success-rate dip > 0.5% over 5m

Quick triage checklist:
1. Check SLO burn chart for the past 1h and 30d.
2. Confirm if new deploy or rollout is in progress (release dashboard).
3. Inspect compute utilization for inference nodes (GPU/CPU).
4. Check model-serving queue depth and rate-limits.
5. Check for recent infra changes (autoscaling events, firewall rules, etc.).

Remediation steps:
1. If a recent rollout is active: rollback or pause canary following the rollout playbook.
2. If queue depth is high: scale-out inference pool (automated scale play) and increase throughput by routing to warm cache.
3. If a small subset of models/routes cause the problem: apply fallback routing to verified model variant.
4. If resource exhaustion: temporarily move low-priority customers to degraded-mode routing and notify CS.

Post-incident tasks:
- Create or update postmortem (see Incident Review Standards).
- Schedule a reliability initiative if root cause requires engineering effort.
- Update runbook with any missing steps discovered during remediation.

Runbook Testing and Health

- Runbooks must be exercised at least twice per year via game-days or runbook drills. Record date and outcome in the runbook metadata.
- Owners must mark runbooks as "last tested" and update steps annually or after major infra changes.

7) Ownership, Escalation & Governance

- Every SLO and runbook must have a named owner (team + primary on-call). Owners are responsible for maintaining dashboards, alerts, and runbook accuracy.
- Escalation matrix: on-call -> SRE lead -> Platform Engineering manager -> CTO for Sev1 incidents.

Governance and Audit

- SRE leadership performs an annual audit of SLOs, runbooks, and capacity forecasts. Findings are published to the eng-sre space and actioned within 90 days.

Appendix A: Sample SLO measurement (PromQL)

- name: api_success_rate_30d
- query: "sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api\",status=~\"2..|3..\"}[30d])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api\"}[30d]))"
- numerator: 2xx/3xx responses over 30d
- denominator: total requests over 30d

Appendix B: Sample Runbook CLI snippet

- Check model-serving pool nodes:
  - ssh ops@serving-node-01 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv"
- Trigger safe scale-out (one-line):
  - rbctl scale pool inference-pool --delta 4 --strategy best-effort
